svg.title: How scholarly data is acquired, checked, and stored
svg.desc: A scout calls a scholarly tool. The request passes the blocked-source policy and the cache, reaches OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, ACL Anthology, or OpenCitations, and returns as a normalized record. The agent's evidence is checked against that tool output and appended to the ledger, then persisted to Postgres and the bibliography.
svg.text: Academic data: request → normalize → cite → check → store
one scholarly tool call, and one refused because the task blocks that source

g.text: A scout calls a scholarly tool. A fetch of a blocked source is refused before any request.
Cache and per-job memo first; then the provider APIs (search hits OpenAlex and arXiv).
Provider records become ScholarWork records: IDs, dates, publication status and its basis.
The agent cites a SourceRef with a verbatim quote; code checks both against its tool output.
The ledger renames claims uniquely; Postgres keeps the ledger and hashed tool events.
